title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of the Company. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test, and the ban on dealing in other companies' securities while possessing inside information about them, but not by the blackout periods, approval regime, margin lending approval, short-term/speculative dealing ban, or hedging ban in section 4, which apply only to Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors; other key management personnel and direct reports to the Managing Director (Senior Executives); and other persons who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions (Nominated Employees). Bound by blackout periods, the prior-approval regime, margin lending approval, the short-term/speculative dealing ban, and the hedging ban.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, including the Managing Director; a subset of Restricted Persons distinguished only for approval routing (Chair of the Board, except for the MD's approval which also goes to the Chair, and except for the Chair's own trading) and for the section 4.8 post-trade confirmation duty.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; a subset of Directors distinguished only because their own approval is sought from the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Other key management personnel and direct reports to the Managing Director; distinguished only for approval routing (Managing Director).

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Persons who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions; distinguished only for approval routing (Managing Director).

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Person in dealings with the Company or Company securities (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, or dependants), or a company or other entity the Restricted Person can control. Does not apply to family members who are financially independent from the Restricted Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities

windows.start_anchor: close of the ASX trading day on 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: 10.00 am (Sydney time) on the ASX trading day following the day on which the Company's half-yearly results are released to ASX

windows.end_anchor: 10.00 am (Sydney time) on the ASX trading day following the day on which the Company's full-year results are released to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a blackout period from time to time. Not stated to be confidential.

rules.detail: There is no formal 'Company securities' definition extending to derivatives, but the Hedging clause catches 'any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities' with no venue limit, so a bank-written OTC put/call is caught. Vesting-state-specific hedging rules apply (see hedging topic); for vested, unrestricted securities the arrangement requires ordinary prior approval under 4.3/4.4.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: The hedging ban and approval regime in section 4 bind only Restricted Persons; ordinary Employees may enter a derivative over Company securities without approval, subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging Company securities acquired under an equity plan before they vest.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired by a Restricted Person under an employee, executive or Director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban extends to vested Company securities that remain subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under an equity plan.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an Employee, Executive or Director equity plan operated by the Company by a Restricted Person.

rules.detail: Section 4.7 only bans hedging while unvested or holding-locked; once vested and free of any holding lock, a hedge is an ordinary dealing requiring prior approval routed via the Company Secretary to the relevant approver.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a trading blackout period under section 4.1 Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed dealing, seek approval for the proposed dealing in the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Section 4.7's hedging ban is an 'additional restriction applying to Restricted Persons'; ordinary Employees are not bound by it.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. It falls within 'otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities' and requires prior approval as an ordinary dealing under 4.3/4.4; if it involves granting security over the shares it also triggers 4.5.
rules.evidence: buy or sell securities in a company, or enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities, or exercise options over securities, or otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities (deal)

rules.detail: Not bound by the section 4.3/4.4 approval regime, which applies only to Restricted Persons; subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Outright ban on speculative dealing including short-selling, with no clearance carve-out.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short-selling. Short selling involves borrowing and selling securities in the hope that they can be bought back at a lower price in the future to close out the short position at a profit.

rules.detail: Section 4.6's short-selling ban is expressed as an additional restriction on Restricted Persons only; short selling by ordinary Employees is not separately addressed.
Securities lending (as lender) is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named but fall within 'any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities' if used to hedge, requiring the same prior approval; a short CFD would also breach the section 4.6 short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Not bound by section 4's hedging or approval provisions.
rules.evidence: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Not banned: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities, or transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account, is expressly permitted subject to prior approval under the 4.4 procedure, which the Company may make conditional (e.g. on the circumstances in which the securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for: (1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Section 4.5 binds only Restricted Persons; ordinary Employees are not required to seek approval to enter a margin loan.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Only encumbrance connected with a margin lending arrangement is addressed, and is permitted with prior approval rather than banned; a charge or lien unconnected to a margin loan is not separately named.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and ... transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: Section 4.5 binds only Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions applying to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Only a 'margin lending arrangement' is expressly addressed (4.5); a broader secured financing arrangement not structured as a conventional margin loan (e.g. a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge of the shares) is not addressed, and it is unclear whether it would fall within 4.5's approval requirement or escape it altogether.
Not addressed for ordinary Employees.

Ban on buying and selling on market within 3 months, and on other short-term dealings such as forward contracts. Carve-out: selling shares received on vesting under an equity plan within 3 months of vesting is not short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts). Selling shares received on vesting of entitlements under an Employee, Executive or Director Equity Plan within 3 months of the vesting date is not a short-term dealing.

rules.detail: Section 4.6's short-term dealing ban is an additional restriction applying only to Restricted Persons.

exceptions.approver: person providing clearance (MD, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order. Approval to deal will only be granted if the Restricted Person's application is accompanied by sufficient evidence (in the opinion of the person providing clearance) that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available in the circumstances.

exceptions.approver: person providing clearance (MD, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: The Company may make its approval of a margin lending arrangement conditional on terms and conditions it sees fit, for example regarding the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.

exemption_authority: Exceptional circumstances (likely severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order) let a Restricted Person deal during a blackout period if not in possession of Inside Information and their application, with sufficient supporting evidence, satisfies the approver (MD, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available; approval will not be granted for any dealing that fails the Front Page Test.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where clearance is otherwise available for the collar's legs, approval can be refused on a purely reputational/perception basis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver, having consulted with members of management as appropriate, may ... impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chair, MD or ARC Chair can attach bespoke conditions to approval of the derivative legs or the margin lending arrangement, such as tenor, disclosure, or unwind triggers.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan account transfer is a dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a margin account to serve as the bank's collateral is itself treated as requiring the same prior approval as entering into the loan arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clause is framed around a conventional 'margin lending arrangement'; whether a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge of the collared shares (not structured as a margin loan) falls within 4.5's approval requirement, or escapes Policy control altogether, is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a Secured Lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is excluded from the blackout, approval and short-term dealing rules, reducing execution risk on enforcement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company will look past the formal labelling of a collar or loan to its economic substance, so structuring to avoid characterisation as 'hedging' or a 'margin lending arrangement' is unlikely to succeed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This clause does not apply to family members who are financially independent from the Restricted Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A financially independent family member could potentially hold the collar or loan without being swept in as a Connected Person, though this is a narrow carve-out.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unlocked shares is achievable for Restricted Persons under this policy, but each leg needs clearance and both can be conditioned by the Company. Section 4.7 absolutely bans hedging of Company securities that are unvested or still subject to a holding lock/dealing restriction under an equity plan, so the collared shares must have fully vested and cleared any holding lock; hedging of vested, unrestricted securities is not separately banned and falls to the ordinary prior-approval regime routed via the Company Secretary to the MD, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee depending on seniority. Margin lending arrangements and transfers of shares into an existing margin loan account both require the same prior approval, which the Company may condition (including on the circumstances in which the shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call), but the clause is framed around a conventional 'margin lending arrangement' and does not address whether a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge instead would fall within (or escape) that requirement. Approval for any leg can be refused or later revoked without reasons (kept confidential if so), lasts only 10 business days, and will not be granted if the dealing fails the Front Page Test; a forced sale by the bank enforcing its security is, however, excluded from the blackout, approval and short-term dealing restrictions. All of section 4's restrictions bind only Restricted Persons - ordinary Employees face none of them, only the general insider trading prohibition.
